text: Square $ABCD$ has sides of length $4$, and $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{CD}$. A circle with radius $2$ and center $M$ intersects a circle with radius $4$ and center $A$ at points $P$ and $D$. What is the distance from $P$ to $\overline{AD}$?
figure: Square ABCD drawn with A at the top left, B at the top right, C at the bottom right and D at the bottom left, so AD is the left side and DC is the bottom side. M is marked as a dot at the midpoint of the bottom side DC. Inside the square, the upper half of the circle with center M and radius 2 is drawn as a semicircular arc from D up and over to C. The arc of the circle with center A and radius 4 is drawn inside the square as a quarter circle from D curving up to B. The two arcs cross at the marked point P, which lies inside the square to the right of center and a little below the middle (about three quarters of the way across and about 40 percent of the way up). No lengths are marked on the diagram.
